sources.note: Nothing on stress; inventories all known materials: 'Scanty notes on Biksi grammar can be found in Laycock & Z'Graggen 1975:740-741, and short wordlists are published in Laycock 1972 and Conrad & Dye 1975. An unpublished SIL survey of Indonesia contains 250-word lists for Yetfa from five locations and 15 sentences in Yetfa (Kim 2006).' Table 1 rates total documentation as 'ca 250 words and 15 sentences'.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. & John A. Z'graggen. 1975. The Sepik-Ramu Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study, vol. 1 (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 731-763. Section 2.11.3.1.1 'Biksi stock-level isolate', pp. 740-741.

sources.note: Nothing. The only published phonological remarks on the language: 'Data on Biksi is too scanty to make definite pronouncements on its nature, but some indication can be given. The phonology lacks a palatal series.. consonants appear to be /p t k b d g m n ŋ f v s r l w y/.. Vowels are /a e i o u/, of which /a e o/ occur nasalised' -- segments and nasalisation only; no mention of stress, accent or tone.
